user.title: What kind of device is it?
user.description: Each HubIR entity is one device in front of one Broadlink remote. Add another for every device you want to control.

climate.title: Add an air conditioner
climate.description: The device code names the file of IR codes to use. Find one in the tables in the documentation, or record your own with the HubIR panel in the sidebar.

data.name: Name
data.temperature_unit: Temperature unit of the recorded codes
data.power_sensor_restore_state: Restore the last mode when the power sensor turns on

data_description.device_code: A number such as 1020. Codes from 90000 up are the ones you recorded yourself.
data_description.controller_data: The remote entity that transmits the codes.
data_description.delay: How long to wait between the codes of a multi-code command.
data_description.temperature_unit: Leave empty to read it from the device file, which is right for almost every device.
data_description.temperature_sensor: Optional. Reports the real room temperature, which infrared cannot.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional. Tells the entity whether the device is really on.

error.cannot_load_device_file: That device file could not be read or downloaded. Check the device code and your internet connection, then try again.
error.invalid_device_file: That device file exists but cannot produce a working entity.
error.unsupported_controller: That device file was recorded for a different kind of hub. This integration only sends through Broadlink.
error.unsupported_encoding: That device file stores its codes in an encoding this integration cannot send.
error.no_operation_modes: That device file lists no operation mode Home Assistant recognises.
error.no_fan_speeds: That device file lists no fan speeds.
error.remote_not_found: That remote entity does not exist.
error.already_configured: Another HubIR entity already uses this device code on that remote.

init.title: Change this device's settings
init.description: Saving reloads the entity, so the changes take effect straight away. The device code and the kind of device are fixed; add another entity to use a different device file.
